scope: Original school-taught Year 2 Chemistry mock only: optical isomerism, aldehydes/ketones, esters and abstract acylation, manually marked drawings
notes: Draw the required answer using on-page sketch or photograph. All diagram/mechanism marking points are SELF-REVIEWED, never inferred from a text match; no use, sourcing, preparation or handling instructions for chemicals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.series: Original AQA-style Organic Chemistry Drawing Practice
questions.question: Draw both enantiomers of butan-2-ol
questions.prompt: Draw a pair of three-dimensional, non-superimposable mirror-image structures of butan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃, using solid wedges and dashed bonds at the chiral carbon. Identify the chiral centre. Use the sketch/photo and manual mark-point checker: this answer requires a drawing. [4 marks]
markPoints: The second carbon is correctly identified as the stereogenic (chiral) centre.
Each structure attaches the four different groups OH, H, CH₃ and CH₂CH₃ to that carbon.
The 3D wedge/dashed-bond arrangement is internally consistent and stereochemically possible in both drawings.
The second structure is the non-superimposable mirror image of the first, with opposite configuration rather than a mere rotation.
questions.modelAnswer: Butan-2-ol has one chiral carbon, C2, bonded to H, OH, CH₃ and CH₂CH₃. Draw tetrahedral wedge/dash structures with all four groups correctly connected, then invert the stereochemistry at C2 to show the enantiomer. Merely swapping the two drawings on the page or rotating one does not create a different enantiomer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.series: Original AQA-style Organic Chemistry Drawing Practice
questions.question: Draw carbonyl reduction arrows
questions.prompt: Draw the nucleophilic addition mechanism in which a hydride nucleophile H⁻ attacks the carbonyl group of butan-2-one, CH₃COCH₂CH₃. Show both curly arrows for the addition step, the charged intermediate and the alcohol formed after protonation. This is a theoretical mechanism question, not a practical procedure. Review the drawing manually. [4 marks]
markPoints: A curly arrow starts at the electron pair of H⁻ and points to the carbonyl carbon, not the carbonyl oxygen.
A second curly arrow goes from the C=O π bond to the oxygen atom.
The tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate has the former carbonyl oxygen labelled O⁻ and a new C–H bond.
Protonation of the alkoxide yields butan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃ (a secondary alcohol).
questions.modelAnswer: Electron pair from H⁻ attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon as the π electron pair moves onto oxygen. This creates the tetrahedral alkoxide CH₃C(H)(O⁻)CH₂CH₃. Protonation yields CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃, butan-2-ol. Do not draw an arrow from the carbonyl C towards H⁻.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.series: Original AQA-style Organic Chemistry Drawing Practice
questions.question: Draw addition–elimination mechanism
questions.prompt: Use generic organic groups R to DRAW the theoretical nucleophilic addition–elimination electron-pair mechanism of water attacking R–C(=O)–Cl. Show the electron-pair arrows, tetrahedral intermediate, elimination step and final carboxylic acid (following deprotonation). Do not give laboratory instructions. Review the drawn mechanism manually. [5 marks]
markPoints: The water oxygen's lone pair attacks the acyl carbonyl carbon; the curly arrow starts from the oxygen lone pair.
A second curly arrow moves the C=O π pair to the carbonyl oxygen.
The tetrahedral intermediate shows carbon bonded to R, Cl, O⁻ and OH₂⁺ with correct formal charges.
The negatively charged oxygen reforms C=O and Cl leaves by a curly arrow from C–Cl bond to Cl.
Deprotonation produces the carboxylic acid R–COOH; chloride leaves as Cl⁻, without retaining an impossible carbon valency.
questions.modelAnswer: At the acyl carbon, H₂O attacks with an oxygen lone pair while the carbonyl π bond moves onto O. The tetrahedral intermediate is R–C(O⁻)(Cl)(OH₂⁺). O⁻ reforms the carbonyl and the C–Cl electron pair goes to Cl, followed by loss of a proton from the protonated product to give R–COOH. This is an abstract explanation of electron-pair movement only.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.series: Original AQA-style Organic Chemistry Drawing Practice
questions.question: Draw and label ethyl propanoate
questions.prompt: Draw a clear displayed or unambiguous structural formula of ETHYL PROPANOATE and identify its ester linkage. On the same drawing label which part comes from the propanoic acid and which part from the ethanol. No preparation conditions are required. Review the structure manually. [4 marks]
markPoints: Correct complete connectivity is drawn as CH₃CH₂–C(=O)–O–CH₂CH₃.
The carbonyl O is double-bonded to the acid-derived carbon; the adjacent ether-like O is single-bonded to the carbonyl C.
The propanoate (acid-derived) section is correctly indicated as CH₃CH₂C(=O)O–.
The ethyl (alcohol-derived) section is correctly indicated as –CH₂CH₃ attached through the ester oxygen, not directly to carbonyl carbon.
questions.modelAnswer: The formula is CH₃CH₂C(=O)OCH₂CH₃. The CH₃CH₂C(=O)O– group derives from propanoic acid; the –CH₂CH₃ attached to the single-bonded oxygen derives from ethanol. The –C(=O)–O– group is the ester linkage, not an ether or a ketone.
